title: Rheumatoid arthritis: early DMARDs and treat-to-target
subject: rheumatology-dermatology
summary: Start a DMARD as soon as RA is diagnosed: methotrexate titrated to at least 15 mg once weekly (usual maximum 25 mg) with folic acid, an optional short glucocorticoid bridge tapered off within about 3 months, and treat to remission or low disease activity; add a biologic (or a JAK inhibitor after risk assessment) if the target is missed by 6 months.

sections.title: Recognise and refer early
items: Persistent synovitis (soft joint swelling) of more than one joint, typically symmetrical small joints of the hands and feet (MCP, PIP, MTP), with morning stiffness over 30 minutes, fatigue and a positive MCP or MTP squeeze test.

Refer suspected persistent synovitis urgently to rheumatology (EULAR: assessment within 6 weeks of symptom onset), even when ESR, CRP and rheumatoid factor are normal. Avoid starting glucocorticoid before assessment where possible, as it masks synovitis.

2010 ACR/EULAR classification: 6 or more of 10 points from joint distribution, serology (RF, ACPA), acute phase reactants and symptom duration of 6 weeks or more. Classification supports but does not replace clinical diagnosis.

Exclude mimics: viral arthritis (parvovirus B19, chikungunya, hepatitis B and C), psoriatic arthritis, SLE, gout or CPPD, polymyalgia rheumatica, hypothyroidism, and hand osteoarthritis (DIP and thumb-base bony swelling).
Poor prognostic features: high RF or ACPA titres, high disease activity and swollen joint count, raised ESR or CRP, early erosions.

sections.title: Investigations and baseline
items: RF and anti-CCP (ACPA), ESR and CRP, CBC, creatinine and eGFR, liver enzymes, urinalysis; ANA if features suggest connective tissue disease.
X-rays of hands and feet at baseline (erosions, periarticular osteopenia); ultrasound can confirm synovitis when examination is equivocal.
Before DMARDs: hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc) and hepatitis C serology, HIV if at risk, chest X-ray, pregnancy test and contraception plan, alcohol history.
Record a validated disease activity score at every visit (DAS28, CDAI or SDAI). Remission: DAS28 below 2.6, CDAI 2.8 or less, SDAI 3.3 or less, or ACR/EULAR Boolean remission.

sections.title: First DMARD strategy
items: Start a csDMARD as soon as the diagnosis is made. Methotrexate should be part of the first strategy (EULAR 2025); use leflunomide or sulfasalazine if it is contraindicated or not tolerated early.

Methotrexate once WEEKLY on a fixed day: titrate to at least 15 mg weekly within 4 to 6 weeks (ACR 2021), usual maximum 25 mg weekly. Oral first; for intolerance or inadequate response, split the oral dose or switch to subcutaneous before changing drug.
Give folic acid with methotrexate (for example 5 mg once weekly on a different day); increase folic acid if GI or mucosal side effects.
Low disease activity (ACR): hydroxychloroquine or sulfasalazine are acceptable first choices; prefer methotrexate with poor prognostic features.

Guidelines differ on bridging glucocorticoid: EULAR advises considering a short course when starting or changing csDMARDs, tapered and stopped as rapidly as feasible (ideally within 3 months); ACR 2021 conditionally advises against routine bridging and strongly against glucocorticoid for 3 months or longer.
Intra-articular glucocorticoid for single troublesome joints (after excluding infection) is a useful adjunct but does not replace DMARD adjustment.

sections.title: Treat to target and escalation
items: Target sustained remission, or low disease activity if remission is unrealistic. Review every 1 to 3 months while active; change therapy if there is no improvement by 3 months or the target is not reached by 6 months.

Target missed on the first csDMARD strategy: EULAR 2025 advises adding a biologic DMARD (TNF inhibitor, abatacept, tocilizumab or sarilumab, or rituximab), preferably with methotrexate. ACR also allows triple csDMARD therapy (methotrexate, sulfasalazine, hydroxychloroquine).

JAK inhibitors (tofacitinib, baricitinib, upadacitinib, filgotinib) may be considered after weighing risk factors: age 65 or more, current or past smoking, other cardiovascular risk factors, malignancy risk and VTE risk. Prefer a biologic when these are present.
If the first biologic or JAK inhibitor fails, switch to another biologic (same or different class) or a JAK inhibitor, considering risks.
Combine biologics and JAK inhibitors with a csDMARD; IL-6 inhibitors and JAK inhibitors have some advantage when no csDMARD can be used.
Sustained remission after glucocorticoid is stopped: continuing DMARDs is preferred (EULAR 2025); cautious dose reduction may be considered, but stopping all DMARDs usually leads to a flare.

sections.title: Screening, high-risk groups and pregnancy
items: Screen for latent TB (IGRA or tuberculin skin test plus chest X-ray) before any biologic or JAK inhibitor and treat latent TB before starting; this matters most in high TB-burden settings.

Hepatitis B (ACR): prophylactic antiviral for anti-HBc positive patients starting rituximab and for HBsAg positive patients starting any biologic or JAK inhibitor; anti-HBc positive, HBsAg negative on other agents need viral load and liver enzyme monitoring. Co-manage with hepatology.

Vaccinate before immunosuppression where possible: influenza, pneumococcal, recombinant (non-live) zoster, hepatitis B if non-immune. Avoid live vaccines on biologics, JAK inhibitors or high-dose glucocorticoid.

NYHA class III or IV heart failure: avoid TNF inhibitors. Previous lymphoproliferative disorder: rituximab preferred. Serious infection in the past 12 months: prefer adding csDMARDs over biologics or JAK inhibitors (ACR).

Pregnancy: methotrexate and leflunomide are teratogenic (stop methotrexate 1 to 3 months before conception; leflunomide needs colestyramine washout). Hydroxychloroquine, sulfasalazine, azathioprine, low-dose prednisolone and certolizumab can be used; plan with rheumatology.

sections.title: Drug safety monitoring
items: Methotrexate, leflunomide and sulfasalazine: CBC, liver enzymes and creatinine every 2 to 4 weeks for the first 3 months and after dose increases, then every 8 to 12 weeks when stable.

Methotrexate: reduce the dose if eGFR is 30 to 60 and avoid below 30; avoid trimethoprim and co-trimoxazole (marrow toxicity); limit alcohol. Urgent CBC and review for mouth ulcers, sore throat, fever, bruising, new cough or breathlessness (pneumonitis).
Hydroxychloroquine: baseline eye examination in the first year, then annual retinal screening after 5 years (sooner with CKD or doses above 5 mg/kg/day).
Leflunomide: also check blood pressure and weight. Periodically assess cardiovascular risk, fracture risk and lung disease (RA-associated ILD).

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Methotrexate taken daily instead of weekly: potentially fatal. Write the day of the week on the prescription and counsel the patient.
Delaying DMARDs while waiting for positive serology: RF and ACPA are negative in a substantial minority of RA.
Long-term glucocorticoid in place of escalating DMARDs.
Starting a biologic or JAK inhibitor without TB and hepatitis B screening.
Attributing fever or new cough on immunosuppression to RA activity: exclude infection (including TB) and methotrexate pneumonitis.

drugs.name: Methotrexate
drugs.dose: Start 10 to 15 mg orally once weekly (7.5 mg if elderly or CKD); increase by 5 mg every 2 to 4 weeks to at least 15 mg weekly within 4 to 6 weeks; usual maximum 25 mg once weekly, oral or subcutaneous
drugs.notes: Weekly only. With folic acid. Reduce if eGFR 30 to 60; avoid below 30, in pregnancy and significant liver disease.

drugs.name: Folic acid
drugs.dose: 5 mg orally once weekly, on a different day from methotrexate
drugs.notes: Reduces GI, mucosal and liver toxicity; can be increased if side effects.

drugs.name: Hydroxychloroquine
drugs.dose: 200 to 400 mg orally daily, not exceeding 5 mg/kg actual body weight per day
drugs.notes: Retinal screening. Reduce dose in CKD.

drugs.name: Sulfasalazine (enteric-coated)
drugs.dose: 500 mg orally daily, increased by 500 mg each week to 2 to 3 g daily in 2 to 3 divided doses
drugs.notes: CBC and liver monitoring; compatible with pregnancy; reversible oligospermia.

drugs.name: Leflunomide
drugs.notes: Teratogenic: before conception give colestyramine 8 g three times daily for 11 days. Monitor BP, liver enzymes, CBC.

drugs.name: Adalimumab (example TNF inhibitor)
drugs.notes: With methotrexate. Screen TB and hepatitis B and C first. Avoid in NYHA III or IV heart failure.

drugs.name: Tofacitinib (JAK inhibitor)
drugs.notes: Only after assessing cardiovascular, malignancy and VTE risk. Monitor CBC and lipids; recombinant zoster vaccine beforehand.
